verdict.rationale: ESD's own guidance acknowledges third-party representation: firms that represent employers can manage 'many tasks' in eServices. That is only a glancing mention and never spells out the permitted versus prohibited actions. The authenticated portal (secure.esd.wa.gov) could not be inspected for further detail. Missing for 10: a published list of what representatives may and may not do, the authorization/power-of-attorney forms, defined delegate roles, and which signatures or attestations must stay personal to the employer.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: Employers and firms that represent employers can manage many tasks in eServices.
